QUAD 33 CONTROL UNIT

Restoring your Quad 33

The 33 is Quad's transistor control unit (preamplifier), usually paired with the 303 power amplifier. It has plug-in boards: a Disc Adaptor board (sets the pickup input: M1 low-output magnetic, M2 high-output magnetic, C1 ceramic, S1 spare), a Tape Adaptor board, a pre-amp board, two amp (tone/volume) boards, a filter board and a power supply board. It runs from a low-voltage supply, but the mains is inside the case and on the rear mains outlets.

Status: Draft recap of all boards, 16 V supply modification, gain reduction, phono gain and MM loading options; not user- or bench-tested; no BOM rows physically verified.

You work from three things

  1. Your unitWhat is actually fitted wins. Quad made running changes, and earlier owners may have too.
  2. The documentsQuad's service data and diagrams, and the DADA and community upgrade guides, listed below.
  3. The AI guideAn AI assistant with the Quad Agent skill cross-checks your unit against the documents and says where they disagree.

Safety first

This unit runs from the mains and can hold a dangerous charge after it is unplugged. If you are new to electronics, use this page to plan and to talk to a qualified technician: do not open the case, solder, measure inside or power it up after work yourself. Read the safety guidance.

Start here

  1. Identify it from the outside. Note the serial number and the details in the table below. Photos of the rear label help.
  2. Ask the AI guide. Load the skill into your AI assistant and paste the prompt below. It will ask you questions before giving any values.
  3. Decide the job. A like-for-like recap restores the unit; the optional upgrades change how it behaves. Choose deliberately.
  4. Plan the parts. Use the provisional parts list below and the documents to check it. Have the actual board checked before ordering.
  5. Get the work done safely. Internal work, adjustment and first power-up belong with a competent restorer or qualified technician.

PROMPT FOR YOUR AI ASSISTANT

Read quad-upgrade/SKILL.md and follow it to help me restore my Quad 33. Start by helping me identify it from the outside.

Give the assistant the skill bundle or the whole quad-upgrade folder.

What to look at

Ask / inspectWhy it matters
Serial numberPlaces the unit in Quad's change history below
Disc and Radio input sockets3-pin DIN before S/N 1225
Which Disc Adaptor position is in use (M1, M2, C1, S1) and the cartridge typeDecides phono gain; DADA's gain changes affect it
Tape Adaptor screw settingsSets tape levels; DADA leaves this as an owner setting
Sources used (CD, streamer, tuner) and power ampDADA's gain reduction is aimed at modern line sources
Mains voltage marked on the rearThe transformer tap must match local mains
Previous repairs or upgradesBoards may no longer match the factory lists
